evidence.claim: Watsco's 2025 Form 10-K states it is the largest distributor of air conditioning, heating and refrigeration equipment and related parts and supplies, with 2025 HVAC/R distribution revenue of $7.2 billion; it also describes a fragmented North American HVAC/R distribution market and the growing importance of the residential replacement market.
evidence.source_title: Watsco, Inc. Form 10-K for fiscal year 2025

evidence.claim: Watsco reported full-year 2025 results in challenging market conditions and said the North American HVAC/R distribution landscape remains highly fragmented with more than 2,100 independent distributors.
evidence.source_title: Watsco Reports Record Full-Year Gross Margin, Meets Inventory Reduction Target and Generates Record 4th Quarter Cash Flow in Challenging Market Conditions

evidence.claim: Ferguson describes itself as North America's largest value-added distributor of essential water and air solutions and says it is integral to repair, maintenance and improvement and new construction projects for residential and non-residential markets.

Ferguson's quarter ended October 31, 2025 release said residential end markets were challenged, new housing starts and permits were weak, RMI remained soft, but U.S. net sales still increased 5.3% with organic revenue growth of 4.4%.

CSW Industrials' fiscal 2026 10-K summary says its Contractor Solutions segment manufactures products for residential and commercial HVAC/R and plumbing applications designed primarily for professional trades, and the HVAC/R industry is driven by replacement and repair of existing systems as well as new construction.
CSW's fiscal 2026 third-quarter release said record revenue and adjusted EBITDA reflected acquisitions that broadened HVAC/R and plumbing product offerings within Contractor Solutions.
evidence.source_title: CSW Industrials Reports Record Results for Fiscal 2026 Third Quarter

evidence.claim: Frontdoor's investor site states the company has more than 50 years of home services experience and more than 75 million service requests, positioning it around home repair and maintenance.
Frontdoor's 2025 annual report says 76% of 2025 home warranty revenue came from existing customer renewals and customers in the renewal channel renewed at an 81% rate.
Invitation Homes reported Q4 2025 total revenues of $685 million and total property operating and maintenance expenses of $245 million, up from $659 million and $228 million respectively in Q4 2024.
evidence.source_title: Invitation Homes Reports Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2025 Results

evidence.claim: Invitation Homes' 2025 10-K summary attributes a 5.4% increase in property operating and maintenance expense partly to a larger average home count and increases in utilities and property taxes; it also notes increased cash used for other capital expenditures for homes.

A March 2026 residential services industry report highlights structural demand drivers including low mortgage-rate lock-in, aging housing stock, housing shortage, aging population and high tappable home equity; it states roughly 70% of homeowners have mortgage rates below 5% and about 50% of U.S. homes are 40+ years old.
evidence.source_title: BGL Consumer Residential Services Insider - March 2026

memory_update.text: WSO, FERG and CSW form a professional-channel repair/remodel supplier cluster across HVAC/R, plumbing and electrical that may be more directly tied to necessary home maintenance than discretionary furnishings.

FTDR is an adjacent home-services platform candidate; inclusion depends on whether recurring warranty renewals and service-call economics can offset claims inflation, contractor-quality risk and weak real-estate transaction channels.
INVH should be tracked as a scaled demand aggregator/customer for single-family rental repairs, turnover work and home-system maintenance rather than as a supplier.

Obvious retailers HD and LOW, appliance/furnishing names, paint/flooring names, and moving/storage companies were not included due to the five-candidate limit and this pass's focus on less obvious second-order beneficiaries.
Need a separate pass for manufacturers upstream of repair channels: HVAC OEMs, water-heater makers, plumbing fixtures, electrical products, roofing, paint, flooring and building-envelope suppliers.

node: Housing-linked consumer spend: home improvement, repair, maintenance, furnishings, rentership, and home services
summary: Expanded universe for the repair/remodel substitution node emphasizes second-order exposure rather than discretionary furnishings. The strongest mappings are professional-channel distributors and contractor-facing suppliers tied to HVAC, plumbing, electrical, water systems, home warranties, and single-family rental maintenance. Initial evidence supports the idea that weak housing turnover and soft big-ticket replacement can still leave pockets of recurring, necessary repair demand, but several candidates need further proof that repair mix offsets housing-cycle weakness.
